claim: The Drosophila tracheal system is a branched tubular network that forms in the embryo by a post-mitotic program of morphogenesis.
source: The Drosophila tracheal system is a branched tubular network that forms in the embryo by a post-mitotic program of morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations to previous work in the introduction.

claim: In third instar larvae (L3), cells constituting the second tracheal metamere (Tr2) reenter the cell cycle.
source: In third instar larvae (L3), cells constituting the second tracheal metamere (Tr2) reenter the cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by previous studies cited in the introduction (Guha and Kornberg, 2005; Guha et al., 2008; Sato and Kornberg, 2002; Weaver and Krasnow, 2008).

claim: Dividing cells in the dorsal trunk, dorsal branch and transverse connective branches respect lineage restriction boundaries near branch junctions.
source: Clonal analysis of L3 Tr2 revealed that dividing cells in the dorsal trunk, dorsal branch and transverse connective branches respect lineage restriction boundaries near branch junctions.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by clonal analysis data presented in Figures 4 and supplements.

claim: Lineage restriction boundaries correspond to domains of gene expression where cells expressing Spalt, Delta and Serrate in the dorsal trunk meet vein-expressing cells in the dorsal branch or transverse connective.
source: These boundaries corresponded to domains of gene expression, for example where cells expressing Spalt, Delta and Serrate in the dorsal trunk meet vein–expressing cells in the dorsal branch or transverse connective.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 2.

claim: Notch signaling was activated to one side of the lineage restriction borders.
source: Notch signaling was activated to one side of these borders and was required for the identity, specializations and segregation of border cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by NRE-lacZ reporter expression in Figure 3.

claim: Notch signaling is required for the identity, specializations and segregation of border cells.
source: Notch signaling was activated to one side of these borders and was required for the identity, specializations and segregation of border cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Notch RNAi experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Tr2 is comprised of developmental compartments.
source: These findings suggest that Tr2 is comprised of developmental compartments and that developmental compartments are an organizational feature relevant to branched tubular networks.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the integration of clonal analysis and gene expression data.

claim: Developmental compartments are an organizational feature relevant to branched tubular networks.
source: These findings suggest that Tr2 is comprised of developmental compartments and that developmental compartments are an organizational feature relevant to branched tubular networks.
evidence: This is a broader conclusion stated in the abstract, extrapolating from the Tr2 findings.

claim: The tracheal primordia have been estimated to derive from approximately ten blastoderm-stage cells.
source: The tracheal primordia, which have 80–90 cells, have been estimated to derive from approximately ten blastoderm-stage cells (Campos-Ortega and Hartenstein, 1985).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: Three post-blastoderm cell divisions have occurred by early stage 11 in tracheal development.
source: Three post-blastoderm cell divisions have occurred by early stage 11, but there are no additional mitoses until L3, when some tracheal cells re-initiate cell cycling (Guha and Kornberg, 2005; Guha et al., 2008; Sato and Kornberg, 2002; Weaver and Krasnow, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous studies.

claim: There are no additional mitoses in tracheal cells between early stage 11 and L3.
source: Three post-blastoderm cell divisions have occurred by early stage 11, but there are no additional mitoses until L3, when some tracheal cells re-initiate cell cycling (Guha and Kornberg, 2005; Guha et al., 2008; Sato and Kornberg, 2002; Weaver and Krasnow, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous studies.

claim: At the beginning of L3, the dorsal trunk has 16-18 cells.
source: At the beginning of L3, the branches of Tr2 are sparsely populated by large cells (Figure 1A). The DT has 16–18, the DB 8, and the transverse connective (TC) 5–7 (Guha and Kornberg, 2005; Guha et al., 2008; Lin, 2009; Weaver and Krasnow, 2008); there is no air sac primordium (ASP).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: At the beginning of L3, the dorsal branch has 8 cells.
source: At the beginning of L3, the branches of Tr2 are sparsely populated by large cells (Figure 1A). The DT has 16–18, the DB 8, and the transverse connective (TC) 5–7 (Guha and Kornberg, 2005; Guha et al., 2008; Lin, 2009; Weaver and Krasnow, 2008); there is no air sac primordium (ASP).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: At the beginning of L3, the transverse connective has 5-7 cells.
source: At the beginning of L3, the branches of Tr2 are sparsely populated by large cells (Figure 1A). The DT has 16–18, the DB 8, and the transverse connective (TC) 5–7 (Guha and Kornberg, 2005; Guha et al., 2008; Lin, 2009; Weaver and Krasnow, 2008); there is no air sac primordium (ASP).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: There is no air sac primordium at the beginning of L3.
source: At the beginning of L3, the branches of Tr2 are sparsely populated by large cells (Figure 1A). The DT has 16–18, the DB 8, and the transverse connective (TC) 5–7 (Guha and Kornberg, 2005; Guha et al., 2008; Lin, 2009; Weaver and Krasnow, 2008); there is no air sac primordium (ASP).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: At late L3, the dorsal trunk has approximately 360 ± 40 cells.
source: At late L3, the DT has approximately 360 ± 40 cells (Lin, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: Re-entry into the cell cycle in the dorsal trunk was synchronous.
source: At 0–2 hr after the L2-3 molt, 22/24 marked cells appeared to be isolated singles without marked neighbors, as would be expected prior to onset of proliferation and for the observed frequency of recombination (11%). At 16–18 hr , 80% were still singles, but at 18–20 hr, 69% were clones of two adjacent cells. This suggests that re-entry into the cell cycle was synchronous and that most DT cells divide according to a similar schedule.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on clonal analysis data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Most DT cells divide according to a similar schedule.
source: At 0–2 hr after the L2-3 molt, 22/24 marked cells appeared to be isolated singles without marked neighbors, as would be expected prior to onset of proliferation and for the observed frequency of recombination (11%). At 16–18 hr , 80% were still singles, but at 18–20 hr, 69% were clones of two adjacent cells. This suggests that re-entry into the cell cycle was synchronous and that most DT cells divide according to a similar schedule.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on clonal analysis data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The cycle time for DT cell divisions at 23°C is 10-12 hours.
source: Divisions continued with approximate synchrony and with cycle time (at 23°C) of 10–12 hr (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on clonal analysis data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The time interval during L3 can accommodate five cell divisions.
source: The time interval during L3 that follows the onset of mitotic cycling can therefore accommodate five divisions, and if all of the starting population contributes to growth, the five divisions are sufficient to produce all the cells in the DT of the wandering L3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on calculation from the observed cycle time.

claim: Five cell divisions are sufficient to produce all the cells in the DT of the wandering L3.
source: The time interval during L3 that follows the onset of mitotic cycling can therefore accommodate five divisions, and if all of the starting population contributes to growth, the five divisions are sufficient to produce all the cells in the DT of the wandering L3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on calculation from cell numbers and division cycles.

claim: DT cells do not tend to migrate or intermix with their neighbors.
source: The clones formed contiguous patches (Figure 1C), indicating that the DT cells do not tend to migrate or intermix with their neighbors; there was no apparent bias to their distribution within the DT.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by clonal analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Sal expression is detected in DT cells but not in cells of the DB.
source: Sal, Ser and Delta expression was detected in DT cells, but not in cells of the DB (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Serrate expression is detected in DT cells but not in cells of the DB.
source: Sal, Ser and Delta expression was detected in DT cells, but not in cells of the DB (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Delta expression is detected in DT cells but not in cells of the DB.
source: Sal, Ser and Delta expression was detected in DT cells, but not in cells of the DB (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There is a distinct expression limit of Serrate-expressing DT cells near the TC junction.
source: There was a distinct expression limit of Ser and Delta-expressing DT cells near the TC junction (Figure 2B,C), but the limit of Sal expression in this region was not as distinct (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There is a distinct expression limit of Delta-expressing DT cells near the TC junction.
source: There was a distinct expression limit of Ser and Delta-expressing DT cells near the TC junction (Figure 2B,C), but the limit of Sal expression in this region was not as distinct (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Serrate is expressed in the medial ASP and in the spiracular branch.
source: Ser was detected in the medial ASP and in the spiracular branch (Figure 2B), and Delta expression was detected in the distal ASP (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Delta expression is detected in the distal ASP.
source: Ser was detected in the medial ASP and in the spiracular branch (Figure 2B), and Delta expression was detected in the distal ASP (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cut is expressed throughout the spiracular branch, TC and the LT, and in the proximal ASP.
source: We detected Cut expression throughout the spiracular branch, TC and the LT, and in the proximal ASP (Figure 2D), Kni expression in the DB, visceral branch and medial ASP (Figure 2E), Wg expression in the spiracular branch (Figure 2F) and Vein expression throughout the visceral branch, ASP, TC and LT and in the proximal DB (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Knirps is expressed in the DB, visceral branch and medial ASP.
source: We detected Cut expression throughout the spiracular branch, TC and the LT, and in the proximal ASP (Figure 2D), Kni expression in the DB, visceral branch and medial ASP (Figure 2E), Wg expression in the spiracular branch (Figure 2F) and Vein expression throughout the visceral branch, ASP, TC and LT and in the proximal DB (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Wingless is expressed in the spiracular branch.
source: We detected Cut expression throughout the spiracular branch, TC and the LT, and in the proximal ASP (Figure 2D), Kni expression in the DB, visceral branch and medial ASP (Figure 2E), Wg expression in the spiracular branch (Figure 2F) and Vein expression throughout the visceral branch, ASP, TC and LT and in the proximal DB (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Vein is expressed throughout the visceral branch, ASP, TC and LT and in the proximal DB.
source: We detected Cut expression throughout the spiracular branch, TC and the LT, and in the proximal ASP (Figure 2D), Kni expression in the DB, visceral branch and medial ASP (Figure 2E), Wg expression in the spiracular branch (Figure 2F) and Vein expression throughout the visceral branch, ASP, TC and LT and in the proximal DB (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2G.

claim: No cells were detected that expressed Kni together with Sal, Ser, or Delta.
source: Although the location of the border appeared to vary between different preparations, we attribute these varied appearances to the way the preparations rotated as they were mounted for viewing and to the fact that proximal/distal position of the border is not precisely the same around the circumference of the branch junction; in no specimen did we detect cells that expressed Kni together with Sal, Ser, or Delta.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on immunohistochemistry observations.

claim: NRE-lacZ expression was detected at both the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions in post stage 16 embryos.
source: We examined stages of embryo development subsequent to fusion of the dorsal trunk (post stage 16), and detected expression of NRE-lacZ at both the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the L3 Tr2, NRE-lacZ expression was detected in the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions, as well as in the ASP, in the TC adjacent to the spiracular and in 1-2 cells of the visceral branch proximal to the TC.
source: In the L3 Tr2, NRE-lacZ expression was also detected in the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions, as well as in the ASP, in the TC adjacent to the spiracular (Figure 3C, D) and in 1–2 cells of the visceral branch proximal to the TC (not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: At the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions, NRE-lacZ expression coincided precisely with the boundaries defined by the expression domains of Cut, Kni, Delta and Sal.
source: At the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions, NRE-lacZ expression coincided precisely with the boundaries that are defined by the expression domains of Cut, Kni, Delta and Sal (Figure 3E–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3E-H.

claim: All of the NRE-lacZ expressing dorsal branch cells expressed Kni.
source: All of the NRE-lacZ expressing dorsal branch cells expressed Kni; all of the NRE-lacZ expressing TC cells expressed Cut.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on co-staining experiments.

claim: All of the NRE-lacZ expressing TC cells expressed Cut.
source: All of the NRE-lacZ expressing dorsal branch cells expressed Kni; all of the NRE-lacZ expressing TC cells expressed Cut.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on co-staining experiments.

claim: Expression of NRE-lacZ in the DB was highest in the cells that abut the Ser/Delta/Spalt expressing DT cells, and it decreased with increasing distance from the boundary.
source: In the DB, expression of NRE-lacZ was highest in the cells that abut the Ser/Delta/Spalt expressing DT cells, and it decreased with increasing distance from the boundary.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on observations of NRE-lacZ expression patterns.

claim: Expression of NRE-lacZ in the TC domain was highest in the cells that are in the DT, and expression decreased with increasing distance from the boundary.
source: Similarly, expression of NRE-lacZ in the "TC domain" was highest in the cells that are in the DT, and expression decreased with increasing distance from the boundary.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on observations of NRE-lacZ expression patterns.

claim: vein expression was highest in the DB cells with the most NRE-GFP expression.
source: vein expression was highest in the cells with the most NRE-GFP expression, but expression of Hindsight and Fizzy-related in the DB was not detected in the cells with highest levels of Notch activation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Expression of Hindsight and Fizzy-related in the DB was not detected in the cells with highest levels of Notch activation.
source: vein expression was highest in the cells with the most NRE-GFP expression, but expression of Hindsight and Fizzy-related in the DB was not detected in the cells with highest levels of Notch activation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3J,K.

claim: Notch signaling may pattern the proximal DB.
source: These results suggest that Notch signaling may pattern the proximal DB.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion in the Results section based on the correlation of Notch activation with gene expression patterns.

claim: 79 marked patches were identified that lined the DT/DB border from one side or other.
source: Of the 79 marked patches that lined the DT/DB border from one side or other, all had many cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1–3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: 87 marked patches were identified that lined the DT/TC border from either side.
source: 87 marked patches were identified that lined the DT/TC border from either side (Figure 4—figure supplement 4–6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Clones that lacked sal function appeared to sort out from their neighbors and to bulge abnormally from the plane of the trunk tube.
source: In contrast to marked control clones in the DT, which integrated with their unmarked neighbors and were not morphologically distinct (Figure 5A), clones that lacked sal function appeared to sort out from their neighbors and to bulge abnormally from the plane of the trunk tube (Figure 5B–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B-F.

claim: sal mutant cells expressed Kni and vein but did not express either Delta or Cut.
source: The sal mutant cells expressed Kni and vein (Figure 5C,D) but did not express either Delta or Cut (Figure 5B,E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B-E.

claim: All sal mutant cells expressed NRE-lacZ.
source: All the mutant cells expressed NRE-lacZ (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Clones that ectopically expressed kni appeared to sort out and expressed vein.
source: We also analyzed clones that ectopically expressed kni, and they also appeared to sort out; and they expressed vein (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: sal function is required for DT identity.
source: This expression signature (vein, Kni, Sal-, Delta-, Cut-) is the same as that of DB cells, suggesting that sal function is required for DT identity and that without sal function or with Kni, they transform to DB identity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the gene expression changes in sal mutant clones.

claim: Without sal function or with Kni, DT cells transform to DB identity.
source: This expression signature (vein, Kni, Sal-, Delta-, Cut-) is the same as that of DB cells, suggesting that sal function is required for DT identity and that without sal function or with Kni, they transform to DB identity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the gene expression changes in sal mutant and kni-expressing clones.

claim: Cells adjacent to Sal-expressing cells in the DB strongly expressed vein.
source: We also analyzed clones that ectopically expressed Sal, and noted three phenotypes associated with clones in the DB. First, cells adjacent to Sal-expressing cells strongly expressed vein (Figure 5H), which is normally expressed at high levels in the DB only by cells near the DB/DT junction that activate Notch signaling (Figure 5C,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Sal-expressing cells in the DB expressed Delta.
source: Second, Sal-expressing cells expressed Delta (Figure 5I), which is normally expressed in Sal-expressing DT cells and not in the DB (Figure 2A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The diameter of the branch in the region affected by Sal-expressing clones in the DB was reduced in the cells that expressed Sal and greater in adjacent regions that expressed vein.
source: Third, the diameter of the branch in the region affected by Sal-expressing clones was reduced in the cells that expressed Sal and greater in adjacent regions that expressed vein (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Clones in the TC that over-expressed sal up-regulated Delta and down-regulated Cut.
source: Clones in the TC that over-expressed sal also up-regulated Delta (Figure 5J) and down-regulated Cut (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5J,K.

claim: sal expression transformed DB and TC cells to a DT identity.
source: The effects of ectopic sal expression in the DB and TC suggest that sal expression transformed their cells to a DT identity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the gene expression changes in sal-expressing clones.

claim: Clones that ectopically expressed Delta in the DB non-autonomously activated vein-lacZ expression and Notch signaling in adjacent cells.
source: Clones that ectopically expressed Delta in the DB non-autonomously activated vein-lacZ expression and Notch signaling in adjacent cells, and the affected regions had a diameter greater than the normal DB (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6A,C.

claim: Regions with Delta-expressing clones in the DB had a diameter greater than the normal DB.
source: Clones that ectopically expressed Delta in the DB non-autonomously activated vein-lacZ expression and Notch signaling in adjacent cells, and the affected regions had a diameter greater than the normal DB (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6A,C.

claim: vein was expressed in DB clones that ectopically expressed NotchACT.
source: vein was also expressed in DB clones that ectopically expressed NotchACT, and the morphology of the region with the mutant cells was abnormal and more characteristic of the expanded proximal DB (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Delta-expressing clones in the DT activated Notch signaling in adjacent cells but did not alter the morphology of the DT.
source: In contrast, Delta-expressing clones in the DT, which also activated Notch signaling in adjacent cells, did not alter the morphology of the DT (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Delta-activated Notch signaling at the DT/DB junction induces vein expression and morphological specialization.
source: Because vein is normally expressed by DB cells in the expanded region at the DT/DB junction, these phenotypes suggest that ectopic over-expression of Delta in the DB transformed adjacent cells to a junction identity and that normally, Delta-activated Notch signaling at the DT/DB junction induces vein expression and morphological specialization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the effects of ectopic Delta expression.

claim: The lumen in the expanded region of the proximal DB is branched.
source: Anti-cadherin staining revealed that the lumen in this region of the wild type DB is branched (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Expression of Notch RNAi had no apparent effect on Delta expression in the DT.
source: We expressed Notch RNAi in trachea (btl-Gal4 UAS-NotchRNAi) and observed that the presence of Notch RNAi had no apparent effect on Delta expression in the DT, but it reduced NRE-lacZ expression to undetectable levels at both the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions, and altered the morphology of the DB (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Notch RNAi reduced NRE-lacZ expression to undetectable levels at both the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions.
source: We expressed Notch RNAi in trachea (btl-Gal4 UAS-NotchRNAi) and observed that the presence of Notch RNAi had no apparent effect on Delta expression in the DT, but it reduced NRE-lacZ expression to undetectable levels at both the DT/DB and DT/TC junctions, and altered the morphology of the DB (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6G.

claim: In the absence of Notch signaling, the proximal DB was not expanded and had the same diameter as other more distal regions of the DB.
source: In the absence of Notch signaling, the proximal DB was not expanded and had the same diameter as other more distal regions of the DB.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on observations of Notch RNAi-expressing trachea.

claim: Notch signaling is required at the DB junction for normal morphogenesis.
source: We conclude that Notch signaling is required at the DB junction for normal morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the effects of Notch RNAi.

claim: Clones that express kni and NotchRNAi in the DT do not sort out but appear to integrate with their neighbors without forming a bulge.
source: Figure 6I shows a DT clone in a preparation that was stained with antibodies against Kni and Sal (which marks nuclei of DT cells). The nuclei in the clone lacked Sal staining (similar to DB cells), and in contrast to clones that ectopically over-express kni in an otherwise normal genetic background (Figure 5G), the clones that also down-regulate Notch do not sort out, but appear to integrate with their neighbors without forming a bulge.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Clones that express kni and NotchRNAi crossed into the DB.
source: The clone also crossed into the DB.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section referring to Figure 6I.

claim: Most or all cells in the early L3 DT contribute to re-population.
source: The results of the clonal analysis reported here supports the idea that most or all cells in the early L3 DT contribute to re-population, and because their descendants can fully account for repopulation, we conclude that there is no other cell type involved.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the clonal analysis results.

claim: There is no other cell type involved in DT repopulation besides the early L3 DT cells.
source: The results of the clonal analysis reported here supports the idea that most or all cells in the early L3 DT contribute to re-population, and because their descendants can fully account for repopulation, we conclude that there is no other cell type involved.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the clonal analysis results.

claim: The cells in the L3 DT constitute an equivalence group.
source: The varied locations and shapes of the clones suggest that the cells in the L3 DT constitute an equivalence group.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the clonal analysis results.

claim: The DT/DB border is a line of clonal restriction.
source: Although 26 other specimens had marked cells on both sides of the DT/DB border (Figure 4—figure supplement 7), these specimens had multiple large patches of marked cells that in combination averaged 34% ( ± 23%, std. dev.) coverage of the DT surface. It is most likely therefore that the patches that meet on either side of the DT/TC border represent more than one clone and therefore are not inconsistent with the model we propose - that the DT/DB border is also a line of clonal restriction.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the clonal analysis results.

claim: The DT/TC border is a line of clonal restriction.
source: And because the number of specimens with marked cells on both sides of the DT/TC border (15/102) relative to those with clones only on one side (DT only (40) TC only (47) = 87/102) is consistent with the expected number of independent clones in the DT and TC domains, we suggest that the DT/TC border is also a line of clonal restriction.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the clonal analysis results.

claim: The clone borders that met the common line of lineage restriction appeared to be straighter than elsewhere.
source: First, the clone borders that met the common line of lineage restriction appeared to be straighter than elsewhere.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on observations of clone morphology.

claim: The line of lineage restriction coincided with DB and DT gene expression domains.
source: Second, the line of lineage restriction coincided with DB and DT gene expression domains.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the correlation of clonal boundaries with gene expression patterns.

claim: sal function is essential in DT cells for their identity.
source: We defined these domains by expression of kni in DB cells and of sal, Ser and Delta in DT cells, and found that sal function is essential in DT cells for their identity and that sal expression in DB cells is sufficient to transform to a DT identity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the sal mutant and overexpression experiments.

claim: sal expression in DB cells is sufficient to transform to a DT identity.
source: We defined these domains by expression of kni in DB cells and of sal, Ser and Delta in DT cells, and found that sal function is essential in DT cells for their identity and that sal expression in DB cells is sufficient to transform to a DT identity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the sal overexpression experiments.

claim: Cells in the DT and DB domains may be regulated by genes with selector function.
source: These analyses suggest that cells in the DT and DB domains may be regulated by genes with "selector" function (Garcia-Bellido, 1975), and establish the coincidence of lineage restriction and the expression domains at single cell resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the gene expression and functional analyses.

claim: The DT/DB border situates a Notch signaling center at this position.
source: These properties suggest that the DT/DB border situates a Notch signaling center at this position.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the Notch reporter expression pattern.

claim: The DT/DB border may be a site of polarity reversal.
source: Both gene expression and morphology appeared to be polarized relative to the DT/DB border – suggesting that this border may be a site of polarity reversal, which is also a defining feature of the A/P compartment border of the wing disc (Chen and Struhl, 1996; Chuang and Kornberg, 2000; Garcia-Bellido and Santamaria, 1972; Lawrence and Morata, 1976; Lawrence et al., 2007; Tabata et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the observed polarization of gene expression and morphology.

claim: Segregation of DT and DB cells depended on Notch.
source: Fourth, the behavior of mutant clones suggests that segregation of DT and DB cells depended on Notch.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the behavior of clones with altered Notch signaling.

claim: Notch signaling is active on both sides of the wing disc D/V border.
source: Notch signaling is also required for the wing disc D/V compartment border (Blair et al., 1994; Cohen et al., 1992; Diaz-Benjumea and Cohen, 1993; Irvine and Wieschaus, 1994; Micchelli et al., 1997; Rauskolb et al., 1999), although the mechanism may not be the same. In contrast to the Tr2 borders where Notch activation is polarized and specific to only one side, Notch signaling is active on both sides of the wing disc D/V border.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to previous work.

claim: These studies are the first to identify developmental compartments in an internal tubular organ.
source: Using this strict definition, the studies reported here are the first to identify developmental compartments in an internal tubular organ.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion of the work.
